instructions: Fresh review of each primary candidate: read dialogue first, then exact cards. Assess all six unchanged criteria and all coach-2.0 gates with turn-specific evidence. For pairs, show whether the Stance changes HOW A pursues the Drive in one interaction. Do not invent missing backstory or assume prior approval. Use the alternate only to assess meaningful differentiation. Report actual reservations. No writer scores or improvement claims are supplied.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: Request an Exception
cards.instruction: Get someone to bend one rule first so you can treat the decision as a precedent.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've parked my bicycle beside your trolley. Indoor parking, of course. Could it stay just this once?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's a cleaning trolley. Your bike can stay only because it's raining.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Cleaning first. I'll note rain as an accepted condition.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Tomorrow it's Jo on the counter. She'll put it back outside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then leave Jo a note: 'Bicycle admitted in rain.' I'll show her that before I show her the bicycle.

beats.text: I crossed out today's date like you. Extension box. Let me submit the form tomorrow as a trial.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I corrected a typo. Nobody's had an extension before.

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: One day. No more.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Write that beside the date. Next time we won't be discussing an untested idea.

cards.title: Record My Contribution
cards.instruction: Get your contribution formally recognized, recorded, or repeated where it cannot be quietly forgotten.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I wrote my name in the margin like you. Contribution logged. Put 'roof repaired by Pat' in the village minutes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was testing a new pen. We all know you fixed it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Pen ready. The minutes weren't there with a ladder; they need telling.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We'll thank you at the party.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: After the roof line, write 'thanks pending' so we remember.

cards.title: Choose the Precedent
cards.instruction: Make someone choose which rule, custom, or prior decision will govern what happens now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've laid my handbook face down like yours. Permit on top. It says eight; the handbook says lock at six. Which governs tonight?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was flattening a curled cover. Keep the front open and lock the back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Cover flat. So the permit governs public access, and the handbook everything else?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. Including the kitchen closing at six.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then are we cancelling the seven-o'clock supper, or does the permit govern kitchens too?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've turned Grandma's chair like yours. Head places settled. Does eldest or birthday child get the head seat?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I turned mine out of the sun. Put two chairs there.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Shade first. Which tradition decides who gets served first?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Serve them together. Except there's only one birthday pudding.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then choose before I bring it in: elders first or birthdays first? I can divide it once somebody's had the wish.

cards.title: Interpret the Custom
cards.instruction: Ask them to apply an ambiguous custom where the wording is unclear. Treat their interpretation as the real test of loyalty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've covered my empty plate like yours. Portion saved. How much lasagne will you leave me for after my shift?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine has food. I was keeping flies off. Our custom says a proper portion, not how big.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Plates protected. Then I'll find out what proper means when it's for me.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your brothers want seconds.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Save mine before you serve those. I'd like being expected home to count before being hungry twice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I raised my hand with you. Support recorded. Our club backs members 'where possible'; will you sign my allotment appeal?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was hailing the bus. That could just mean wishing you luck.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Transport first. You get to interpret it. I'd like to know whether membership reaches as far as your signature.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Some members want my name kept off it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then whose comfort does 'possible' protect? Put your name beside mine if it includes me.

cards.title: Withdraw the Objection
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to drop a complaint, challenge, or special request and accept the official process.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've taken a number like you. Claims open. Drop the demand to question our delivery driver; use this missing-parcel form.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was buying a raffle ticket. Your form requires a photo of the parcel I haven't received.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tickets ready. Use a photo of your empty doorstep; that's the delivery location.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Will you stand in it holding today's newspaper?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes, beside the doormat. Put me under supporting evidence and leave the driver off your witness list.
